Subject: Important Notice About Prize Claim Scams
Dear Recipient,
You may receive messages claiming that you have won a large lottery prize but must first pay a processing fee, tax, insurance charge, or transfer cost before receiving funds. This is a common sign of fraud.
Legitimate lotteries and sweepstakes do not ask winners to send money in advance to collect a prize. Requests for payment by cryptocurrency, wire transfer, gift cards, or other hard-to-reverse methods are especially suspicious.
Warning signs include:
unexpected notifications that you entered or won a contest you do not remember joining
pressure to act immediately or keep the matter secret
requests for personal financial information
poor grammar, inconsistent branding, or unofficial email addresses
instructions to pay via bitcoin or another irreversible method
If you receive such a message, do not send money or share personal information. Contact the lottery organization directly using contact details from its official website.
Sincerely,
Consumer Fraud Awareness Team
